discovery: Programmable arrays of individually trapped Rydberg atoms for quantum simulation and quantum information processing

nominees.name: Antoine Browaeys
nominees.affiliation: Laboratoire Charles Fabry, Institut d'Optique / CNRS, Université Paris-Saclay, France

subfield: Atomic, molecular and optical physics / quantum information
motivation: Over two decades, individual neutral atoms held in optical tweezers and coupled through Rydberg interactions have gone from a delicate curiosity to one of the most powerful platforms for controlling quantum matter. Saffman and co-workers demonstrated Rydberg blockade and the first neutral-atom entangling gates, building on the theoretical proposals Lukin co-authored. Browaeys established deterministic assembly of defect-free atom arrays in arbitrary geometries and used them as programmable quantum simulators of spin models. Lukin's group scaled these systems to hundreds of atoms, observing quantum phase transitions, many-body scars and topological spin liquids, and recently realised logical qubits with error correction on reconfigurable arrays. Together they turned the Rydberg blockade into a general tool, giving physics a new laboratory for strongly interacting many-body quantum systems and a leading route to quantum computation. This work unites clean atomic physics, conceptual clarity and technological impact.
